emma_support: Hey folks — customer (kevin) seeing intermittent SSE stream cut after ~90–120s, then a 401 on the next reconnect. They grabbed a curl snippet but it looks like it was simplified. request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, region: us-west-2. Can we create a minimal, validated curl reproduction and a short checklist for them?

dan_engineering: Thanks — can you paste the original curl they ran and the server-side trace for req_0a1b2c3d? Even partial headers help (Authorization, Cookie, Host).

kevin_customer: pasted: ``curl -i -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-stream"`` then it just stops streaming, reconnect returns 401. server log for req_0a1b2c3d shows: `auth: token_expired_window=120s, cookie_present=true, upstream=proxy-a1`

emma_support: OK. Two likely suspects: (1) the token/cookie expiry overlap, (2) an intermediary (proxy/load balancer) closing idle connection. Let's get a minimal curl that: forces HTTP/1.1, disables buffering, includes full headers, and reproduces SSE handshake. I'll propose a snippet — please validate and try it back to customer: 

emma_support: ```
# minimal SSE repro (include verbose headers)
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Cookie: session=<SIGNED_COOKIE>" \
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-stream&stream=true"
```

nate_sre: A few validation additions: (a) run with `-v` so we can see `> GET`/`< HTTP/1.1` headers, (b) capture --trace-ascii to a file if possible, (c) try `--resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.120.55.66` to bypass DNS LB to rule out region-specific LB. Also add a quick loop to hit `curl` repeatedly with small backoff to see if expiry aligns: ```for i in 1 2 3; do curl ...; sleep 30; done```

kevin_customer: I'll try but can you confirm whether we should include `Expect:` or chunked headers? My support engineer suspected proxy removed `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`.

dan_engineering: For SSE the client shouldn't set Transfer-Encoding. Curl will handle chunking; keep `--no-buffer` to stream. If proxy strips chunked it usually still proxies the connection but buffers until close. Key checks for them to send back: full verbose output, server `Date`, `x-request-id` and any `x-proxy-terminate` header. ask them to redact PII but keep trace ids.

emma_support: I'll send the repro + checklist to customer. Checklist to request back:
- run the exact curl above with `--no-buffer --http1.1 -v` and attach the terminal output
- if possible capture `--trace-ascii trace.txt` and attach that file
- time the run and note when streaming stops
- include the `x-request-id` and upstream proxy id from server logs (we already have req_0a1b2c3d)
- try `--resolve` to bypass DNS LB and report difference

kevin_customer: Got it. One more: should they try removing Cookie to force bearer-only auth?

nate_sre: Yes, ask them to test: (A) Authorization header only, (B) Cookie only. If cookie is signed with short TTL it might be expiring at the reconnect window. Also recommend checking the client's system clock drift — signed cookies can fail if clock skew > 60s.

emma_support: I'll collect results and attach here once they respond. If they return verbose output with `x-proxy-terminate` or `401` and matching server trace, we can escalate to infra with traces + curl output.

deploy-bot: patch/stream-keepalive-tuning deployed to staging (rollout id r-2026-03-17-12) :rocket:

dan_engineering: Nice — once kevin confirms reproduction we can try a test against staging to replicate under the same LB config.

kevin_customer: Thanks, I'll run tests and post logs (redacted) later today.

emma_support: Perfect — tagging infra on escalation path if they need deeper packet captures. :thumbsup:
